audio_caption: Two male speakers are having a conversation. The first speaker references a past conversation from December, recalling Bitcoin's value at that time, and mentions the other speaker's bullish outlook. He points out that Bitcoin is now worth around 200% more and asks if the current surge could be a temporary fluctuation. The first speaker has a more neutral, inquisitive tone, while the second speaker sounds slightly more confident.

The audio begins with a male speaker confidently predicting Bitcoin will reach $250,000 by 2022 or 2023, acknowledging potential fluctuations while asserting Bitcoin's inherent value compared to other currencies he believes are slowly losing value. He states, "one bitcoin is still worth one bitcoin" while mentioning other currencies are "drifting away and becoming useless."

The clip begins with a male speaker expressing a desire for a future where "we don't have to pay the credit card companies."  His tone is declarative and speculative.  He immediately corrects himself, clarifying it is "not the credit card companies, it's the banks", and describes them as "trying to gang up and get rid of Bitcoin" with a tone of disapproval.

A male speaker discusses blockchain, describing it as distributed, keeping perfect records, and transparent. He believes it will change the nature of accounting, and accountants may feel threatened. He emphasizes that technology usually wins out, highlighting blockchain as one of the world's great technologies that will benefit everyone.

A man's voice speaks in a confident, speculative tone, forecasting fluctuations and the potential for Bitcoin to reach at least "5% market share." He suggests this outcome would equate to "a $250,000 token."

The audio begins with a man speaking in a conversational tone, summarizing a recent interview with economist Nouriel Roubini, who claims Bitcoin is less secure than fiat currency, emphasizing that "if you lose your credit card details, then you can still get refunded" but with crypto funds "gone forever." He then asks for another person's opinion on the subject. A brief pause follows.

The clip features a single male speaker who sounds somewhat exasperated, correcting someone else's statement about financial matters. He argues that banks aren't responsible for refunding money over a certain amount and highlights the Bitcoin blockchain's security compared to vulnerable banks, suggesting they are constantly fighting off hackers. The speaker implies banks' technology is becoming outdated.

The audio clip features a male speaker discussing the security of Bitcoin blockchain. He mentions that it has never been hacked and emphasizes its rising popularity with the best engineers working to improve it. He notes a shift away from traditional banking systems and suggests that the best security will be found with Bitcoin. The speaker's tone is informative and enthusiastic.

The clip begins with one male speaker discussing economists who, after writing their books, are resistant to change even when faced with evidence suggesting their work needs updating, mentioning "I wrote my book, this is what I've taught everybody" and "I'm never going to change it". He argues that these individuals have a vested interest in maintaining the status quo. He concludes with "progress moves ahead" and advising them to "write another book."

The audio clip begins with a conversation about Libra, Facebook's cryptocurrency. One person is asking another person about their stance on the new project, noting people are excited but concerned about privacy issues that have affected Facebook's reputation. A male speaker expresses they "always welcome innovation," noting the tried and tested Bitcoin, but adds Libra is new and there's some risk to it. He expresses the value of currencies is being decentralized, whereas with Libra, you have to trust Facebook, especially if Zuckerberg isn't around.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker stating that, given the choice between Bitcoin and Libra, he prefers "Bitcoin." He continues, expressing his desire for "a currency that is tried and true," "battle tested," "decentralized, open, transparent, and global." The speaker sounds conversational.

The audio clip presents a male speaker who, in a casual tone, discusses investments in various crypto projects, including OpenNode for Bitcoin usage, decentralized technologies like "gun or party," and "Unstoppable" for censorship-resistant social media. He mentions investments in decentralized bandwidth and websites. The overall soundscape primarily features the speaker's voice.

The clip starts with a male speaker requesting information about a vetting process, inquiring about characteristics that attract attention. Another male voice responds, emphasizing that a lot of it involves the team and the technology, stating the technology has to be "unique and open and new." This speaker describes fundamental changes to the world, making a fundamental impact, differentiating a project from something that's been seen many times before. He states, "If it's just another token," centralized around a company or people, "we don't want to do that." He concludes by mentioning what they would be interested in instead.

The clip begins with a male speaker who is reflecting upon what makes a token "interesting," with references to "smart contracts" and facilitating Bitcoin use. His tone is conversational and measured. The discussion ends on a note of possibility, suggesting "you've got a chance." Lastly, there is a musical string note at the very end.

The audio clip starts with two people speaking. The first one is a male who asks another person to disclose what percentage of their wealth is put in crypto, referencing someone holding more than 50% of their wealth in Bitcoin. The second one is also a male, but with a different tone, stating "I have no idea" and that "when you count your money, it's time to sell everything." He adds "I'm on the rise" and that they take Bitcoin for tuition and rent in their incubator.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker stating that they accept Bitcoin "for anything". A male speaker, possibly different from the first, then promotes subscribing to a channel to find out when Bitcoin will reach the moon. A female voice then says "Coin Telegraph, like, subscribe, and hodl". The clip concludes with a short musical jingle.
